//: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for per-phase model targeting across every coding tool.
Nothing else in this repo may name a model; scripts/check-agent-skills.sh fails on drift.
`claude` and `cursor` name REAL VENDOR TIERS on purpose. Both tools bill against the
developer's seat rather than through a metered API, so these phases should use the capacity the
subscription already includes — it costs nothing marginal. Aliasing them would route
paid-for capacity to a metered endpoint, which is strictly worse.
Concretely, a Cursor seat is TWO pools and they are not equal: first-party (grok /
composer) is generous; third-party (including Anthropic-through-Cursor) is small, and
overflow runs one way only. So the `cursor` column names a first-party Cursor model,
not whatever the `claude` column happens to hold. If Cursor is where you run Anthropic
models, stop — move that work to Claude Code, or switch the Cursor model to grok.
The two columns are chosen PER TOOL and deliberately NOT derived from one another:
keying Cursor off the Claude tier means a Claude-side bump silently retargets Cursor.
`opencode` holds OpenCode provider/model ids (`<provider>/<model>`): xAI Grok through a
SuperGrok login (`/connect` in OpenCode, then `opencode models xai` to see what the login
exposes). It is the fall-through when a Claude or Cursor seat runs dry — same repo, same
harness, same five phases, no tool-hop and no lost context. `opencode_variant` is the
reasoning variant every OpenCode agent runs at. OpenCode reads it as a SEPARATE `variant`
field; never write `xai/grok-4.7#xhigh`, which OpenCode looks up as one catalog key and fails.
A phase MAY deliberately pin a different tier from its siblings — see test-author below.
The manifest exists so that such a choice is STATED and reviewable, not so that every
phase matches. A uniform column is not the goal; an explained column is. That is
ENFORCED: check-agent-skills fails when a `claude` or `cursor` value differs from what
the other phases use and no rationale["<agent>.<column>"] explains it. A rationale that
no longer describes a live deviation fails too. The `opencode` column is exempt:
per-phase role aliases differing IS its intended shape.
`readonly` says the agent MUST NOT EDIT FILES — nothing more. Phases 4 and 5 still run
commands (Vitest, npm run check). OpenCode frontmatter denies edit and leaves bash.
Every `readonly` value must be a JSON boolean — a string like "false" used to coerce
to WRITABLE on one tool and read as false on another.

rationale.test-author.claude: Deliberately claude-opus-4-8, NOT the current opus. Opus 4.8 translates a SPEC into tests with tighter scope discipline: it covers the stated scenarios without inventing adjacent ones. Newer tiers enlarge test scope unprompted, and an over-broad test suite is itself a slop generator — phase 3 then implements behaviour nobody specified. Do not 'upgrade' this to follow the other four phases without re-measuring scope creep.
